quote: Area A to the north of the spring
notes: The spring of ʿEin Feshkha. Keyed so that relations can point to it: Area A lies c. 100 m north of it, Area B in the cliff to its west. No attribute of the spring itself is stated.

period: Early Roman (built under Herod; destroyed c. 130 CE)
quote: fairly large (external dimensions: 18 24 m.; 432 sq.m. in area
notes: Printed '18 24 m.' (the × sign is lost in the text extraction); length_m = longer side throughout this file. height_m = preserved wall height ('2 m. or more'). Exterior walls 1 m thick, fieldstones with mortar; doorways of Samra-sandstone ashlars. Two entrances in the east façade W3 (main 0.7 m to courtyard; additional 0.6 m to northern wing). Room floors of tamped stones 0.2-0.3 m thick. Staircase in southern wing implies upper storey. The 100 m north of Feshkha is stated for the site remains as a whole.

quote: The courtyard is fairly spacious (7.8x11.8 m.; 92 sq.m. in area)
notes: Printed 7.8x11.8 m. Floor of tamped clay at -386.00 m. One square pillar (1x1 m) at its western end, thought to carry the upper-storey terrace, so the west end may have been roofed. The main entrance in W3 leads directly into it.

quote: At its western end a square pillar (lxl m.) is preserved
notes: Printed '1x1 m.' (OCR 'lxl'). At the western end of the courtyard.

quote: there is a main entrance (0.7 m. wide), leading directly into the courtyard
notes: In the façade wall W3, which faces east. Doorways of the building are built of ashlars (general statement, p. 44).

quote: an additional entrance (0.6 m. wide), leading into the rooms of the northern wing
notes: In east façade W3. Author compares Qumran: subsidiary entrance for storage and animals. The text does not say whether this is the same as the common entrance of the two eastern rooms of the northern wing (p. 53); keyed separately.

quote: In the north-western corner (Locus 117) there was a small cell (2.2x2.8 m.)
notes: Printed 2.2x2.8 m. In NW corner of courtyard; divided in two by partition wall W19; rough walls W17, W18 suggest later addition. De Vaux's Locus 6 (storage jar buried to its shoulders): storeroom or pantry. Opus sectile tiles on its floor (p. 45).

period: Early Roman (separating wall a later addition)
quote: Locus 154, a long, narrow room (1.8x8 m.)
notes: Printed 1.8x8 m. At the NE corner of the courtyard, separated from it by wall W13 (perpendicular to the façade, carelessly built, later). Stone mortar in its corner.

quote: The interior space of the mortar is conical, with a depth of 0.3 m.
notes: Conical interior; probably for food processing. In the NE corner of the courtyard, in the corner of L154.

quote: a flight of six stairs (fig. 7) is preserved in the southern wing
notes: Staircase 0.9 m wide in the southern wing, a room on each side (L118 east, L106/L114 west); evidence for an upper storey.

quote: The eastern room, Locus 118, is spacious (4.3x5.6 m.)
notes: Printed 4.3x5.6 m. Southern wing, east of the staircase.

quote: the long, narrow western room (3x8.8 m.) is divided into two loci (106 and 114)
notes: Printed 3x8.8 m. Southern wing, west of the staircase; divided into Loci 106 and 114 by the narrow partition wall W16 (keyed as one room).

quote: The façade wall (W5), preserved to a height of 2.2 m., contains a single doorway
notes: Façade of the western wing (the wing west of the courtyard; higher standard of building, large stones 0.8 m long, thickened foundations). Its single doorway opens into the southern of the wing's two rooms.

quote: The doorway (0.9 m. wide) is built of ashlars with marginal dressing
notes: A stone step in front of the threshold (keyed as 1 step, outside). Triangular lamp niche in the southern jamb, inner face. The text does not state which way the doorway faces.

quote: This small niche (base width: 18 cm.; height: 18 cm.;
notes: Depth 10 cm. Hewn in the southern door jamb on the inner face of the wall, 0.9 m above the floor; lamp niche. width_m = base width.

quote: a single doorway which opens into the southernmost of the two rooms
notes: Southern room of the western wing; no locus number or size given. Openings counted: the W5 doorway and the W6 doorway (0.8 m) to L104.

quote: the western wing was preserved to a height of 1.5 m.
notes: Divides the two rooms of the western wing.

quote: A doorway (0.8 m. wide) provided access to the northern room (Locus 104)
notes: In W6. Facing not stated.

quote: the largest architectural space in the building (internal dimensions: 3.8 8.4 m.;
notes: Printed '3.8 8.4 m.' internal (× lost in extraction); 32 sq m. Basalt lower grinding stone (0.36 x 0.65 m, 0.1 m thick) on the floor near the NW corner (de Vaux's Locus 3): perhaps a kitchen. Iron awl on floor. n_openings counts the one doorway mentioned (in W6).

quote: fairly large (internal dimensions: 3.8x8 m.), apparently served as a stable
notes: Westernmost of the three rooms of the northern wing, 'whose doorways face south, towards the courtyard'. Openings counted: its doorway onto the courtyard (later blocked) and the large window in the south wall W7. Divided by thin partition W10 into L105 (west, burnt) and an eastern part for animals.

quote: In the larger western space (Locus 105), signs of
notes: West of partition W10 in the stable; signs of fierce fire (wall stones cracked and reddened; perhaps a stored straw pile). Only relation to its parent given.

quote: The opening onto the courtyard was blocked at some later phase
notes: Direction from the statement that the northern-wing doorways face south. Blocked later (cf. p. 42 'the blocking of one of the doorways').

quote: large window (0.8 m. wide; at least 0.8 m. high)
notes: Height 'at least 0.8 m'. In the southern wall W7, opening directly onto the courtyard; sill 0.7 m above the raised courtyard level; holes in jambs for tethering; a manger on the sill is suggested. Iron arrowhead embedded in W7 nearby (p. 55).

quote: In the courtyard in front of the window there is a kind of ramp
notes: To ease access to the stable window.

quote: To the east of the stable are two rooms with a common entrance
notes: Common entrance of the two rooms east of the stable (northern wing). Hoard of eight coins of Mattathias Antigonus under its threshold (also p. 42). Direction from the statement that the northern-wing doorways face south. The two rooms themselves have no stated attributes and are not keyed.

quote: three tombs, one next to the other, along the outer face of the southern wall
notes: Found by de Vaux in 1958 (Donceel 2002); one row for the three tombs (no labels or sizes given). Author suggests pagan use.

quote: The industrial complex (fig. 18) is located to the north-east of the main building
notes: Enclosed area c. 2,000 sq m (outer yard or agricultural plot), NE of main building, bounded by fence walls W20-W22. Contains four channels, pool L133, reservoir, stone surface and the installation.

quote: The western fence wall (W20), which runs north-south and is 12 m. long
notes: Starts at the NW corner of the main building, runs N-S. The two fence walls are preserved to 'about 1 m' (height_m) and 0.7 m wide; original height reconstructed c. 2 m.

quote: is 17 m. long and runs east-west in general direction
notes: Perpendicular to W20; the northern fence wall, crossed by channels L135 and channel_2. Preserved about 1 m.

quote: this segment is designated W22 and is preserved for a length of only 3 m.
notes: Southward turn at the east end of W21; probably continued south and west to join the wall perpendicular to the square enclosure.

quote: one of these channels (Locus 135) is approximately 10 m. long
notes: Length 'approximately 10 m'. From a now dried-up spring to the north; crosses fence wall W21. All four channels are fieldstone, plastered with whitish hydraulic plaster.

quote: and the other is 1.5 m. long
notes: Second of the two channels from dried-up springs crossing W21; no locus number given.

quote: Locus 133, a small, well-preserved square pool (1.7x1.7 m.; c. 1 m. deep)
notes: Depth 'c. 1 m'. Two channels drain into it; two lead out (longer to reservoir, shorter to installation). Plaster of the pool itself not stated.

quote: The third channel (10 m. long; 0.5 m. wide) leads to the north-western corner
notes: The longer channel out of L133; to the NW corner of the reservoir; set in the smooth stone surface (paving at -386.00 m). No locus number given.

quote: is rectangular (3.2x8 m.). It is at least 3 m. deep
notes: Printed 3.2x8 m; depth 'at least 3 m' (full depth not excavated). Walls 0.8 m thick. Capacity 'at least 80 sq.m.' (sic). n_steps 0: 'no staircase was found'; hence taken as storage, not bathing. Plaster not stated. No locus number given.

quote: The fourth channel (Locus 137; 2.5 m. long) fed the installation
notes: The shorter channel out of L133; set in the smooth stone surface. The channel to the eastern-cell pool branches off it.

quote: Both channels are integrated in a smooth stone surface
notes: Paving at -386.00 m, about the level of the main-building courtyard. De Vaux found two cylindrical stones on it, west of the large pool.

quote: a large pool with two adjacent cells, western and eastern
notes: Large pool L142 with western cell L127 (gathering vat) and eastern cell L119 (small pool / miqweh). Author: balsam perfume-essence production (de Vaux: tannery).

quote: The large pool (Locus 142) is almost square (4.4 4.5 m.; 1.3 m. deep)
notes: Printed '4.4 4.5 m.' (× lost in extraction). Walls c. 1 m thick. Patches of whitish hydraulic plaster on floor and walls. Two steps in the western wall W33 give access to the floor. Cylindrical stone (1.48 m long, 0.6 m diam.) on the floor near the steps. Drainage opening at the base of the southern wall W29; tunnel under W29 to the gathering vat. Interpreted as soaking pool.

quote: stone drums with a round hole (10 cm. in diameter) that could be blocked
notes: At the base of the southern wall W29; controlled the water level in the pool.

quote: a tunnel that ran under the partition wall (W29) into the gathering vat
notes: Runs under wall W29.

quote: The western cell (Locus 127) is fairly small (2.3x3.5 m.; 8 sq.m. in area)
notes: Printed 2.3x3.5 m. Plastered floor on a foundation of flat tamped fieldstones. Openings: three steps (0.8 m wide) in the southern wall W31 leading down to the floor, and a doorway (0.6 m) in the northern wall W29 to pool L142 (directions from the walls named). Gathering vat in the floor by the eastern wall W36.

quote: three steps, 0.8 m. wide, lead down to the cell's floor
notes: In the southern wall W31.

quote: An additional doorway, 0.6 m. wide, in the cell's northern wall (W29)
notes: Direct access from the cell to the pool to its north.

quote: The vat is square (0.9x1 m.; 1.4 m. deep; capacity: 1.26 cu.m.
notes: Printed 0.9x1 m. In the floor close to the eastern wall W36. A small protruding stone in W36 aids descent (not called a step; n_steps blank). Column drum (0.3 m diam., 0.35 m high) on the floor. No connection with the pool in L119 across W36. Plaster not stated.

quote: a channel (1.1 m. long; 10x20 cm. in section), leading directly from the large pool
notes: Section 10x20 cm; the text does not say which figure is width and which depth, so neither is keyed. A flat, slightly protruding stone at its end stops spillage.

quote: The eastern cell (Locus 119; internal dimensions: 2.8x3.7 m., i.e. 10.3 sq.m.)
notes: Printed 2.8x3.7 m internal. Accessed by four steps (0.6 m wide) leading down from the NW corner (facing not stated). Floor a little lower than the western cell. Small pool in the floor against W36. Fig. 25 caption calls this the 'southern cell'.

quote: accessed by four steps, 0.6 m. wide, leading down from the north-western corner
notes: The channel feeding the pool runs through these steps.

quote: The pool (1.5 1.8 m.; 0.9 m. deep; capacity: 2.4 cu.m
notes: Printed '1.5 1.8 m.' (× lost). Narrow staircase 0.4 m wide inside; only the topmost step preserved (n_steps = preserved), author assumes two more. Called a miqweh by the author on account of the steps (excavator's label). Plaster not stated.

quote: a narrow staircase (0.4 m. wide) permitting descent to the floor
notes: Only the topmost step preserved; two more assumed by the author.

quote: The channel runs around the northern and eastern walls of the large pool
notes: Branches off L137; passes through the steps of the eastern cell.

quote: The enclosure consists of a square yard (34x34 m.; 1,156 sq.m.)
notes: Excavated by de Vaux; mostly obliterated by Route 90. Walls 0.7 m thick. Entrance 'apparently' in the eastern wall facing the main building. Row of 'about ten' pillars c. 2 m apart along the north side (n_pillars 10 for 'about ten').

quote: long narrow space between the pillars and the outer wall of the enclosure (3.5x27 m.)
notes: Printed 3.5x27 m. Between the row of pillars and the outer wall on the north side; probably a stable.

quote: The entrance to the room is on the east
notes: Internal 3x3.5 m (as printed); at the eastern end of the stable; accommodation or storage.

quote: exposed for a length of 12 m., starts at the south-eastern corner
notes: Runs NE from the SE corner of the square enclosure toward the wall east of the industrial complex; probably joined it to bound the yard east of the main building.

quote: join to form a stretch of c. 500 m., roughly north-south in direction
notes: Length 'c. 500 m' for the joined segments. Starts at the NW corner of the square enclosure, runs north toward Qumran; taken by the author as a continuous estate fence wall. in_window from the author's Early Roman date.

quote: runs north for approximately 200 m. towards Qumran
notes: Southern segment, from the NW corner of the square enclosure.

quote: the 110 m. long segment that runs south from the complex of Qumran
notes: Northern end of the long wall.

quote: The structure is square in plan (4.7x4.7 m.; fig. 28). Its walls, 0.8 m. thick
notes: Area B, in the cliff west of the spring, c. 50 m above the Early Roman site (elevation -336 m); vertical difference not put in rel_distance. Walls 0.8 m thick of roughly squared limestone blocks (0.7x1 m average); east wall eroded; fill 0.5-1 m over an ash layer. Maʿaleh Feshkha path runs to its west.

quote: A steep path named Macaleh Feshkha climbs to the south-west from cEin Feshkha
notes: Ascent for pedestrians and pack animals to the Hyrcania valley and Jerusalem; climbs SW; runs to the west of the Area B tower.

quote: two springs, cEnot Qumran (Arabic: cEin Ghazal) and, c. 800 m. to the south, Tannur
notes: South of Nahal Qumran, east of Route 90. Distance 'c. 800 m'. Bearing = from the related feature to this one.

quote: c. 800 m. to the south, Tannur (Arabic: cEin et-Tannur)
notes: East of Route 90. Distance 'c. 800 m'.

quote: This was a square enclosure (c. 17 17 m.; 290 sq.m.)
notes: Printed 'c. 17 17 m.' (× lost). c. 200 m south of Nahal Qumran and c. 80 m west of the road (neither keyed). Wall of large fieldstones (0.4x0.5 m average) laid without mortar; estimated original height c. 2 m, upper part perhaps mudbrick. Not dated in this text.

class_as_printed: segment of its north western corner
quote: A c. 20 m segment of its north western corner has been preserved
notes: Length 'c. 20 m'; two courses preserved, to 0.6 m.

quote: a square structure (12x12 m.) with an entrance on the east
notes: c. 25 m NW of ʿEnot Qumran, close to the modern road; little survives, description after de Vaux. Walls 1.1 m thick; interior divided by a partition wall; 'pillar-like constructions' in the NE and SE corners to strengthen it (n_pillars 2). Author suggests a columbarium (fig. 31 caption 'columbarium?'); class kept as building. Undated in the text; linked by the author to an Early Roman estate.
